title: Methods for Electroporation and Transformation Confirmation in Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM20016
protocol: Inoculate L. reuteri from glycerol stock into 6 mL of MRS broth.
Incubate the culture aerobically overnight at 37°C in a static incubator.
Inoculate 4 mL of the overnight culture into 200 mL of MRS broth (1:50 dilution).
Allow the culture to grow aerobically until OD600 reaches 0.5-0.85.
Decant the media and place the tubes on ice while balancing them.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 5,000 x g in a pre-chilled (4°C) centrifuge.
Discard supernatant and resuspend each pellet in 50 mL of pre-chilled ddH2O.
Centrifuge again at 5,000 x g for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend each pellet in 25 mL of ddH2O: 0.5 M sucrose, 10% glycerol.
Centrifuge the mixture at 5,000 x g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend all pellets in 2 mL of ddH2O: 0.5 M sucrose, 10% glycerol.
Aliquot cells into 50 µL to 100 µL portions in pre-chilled microcentrifuge tubes.
Store aliquots at -80°C for later use.
Take an entire electrocompetent L. reuteri aliquot and thaw it on ice.
Gently mix 5 μL to 10 μL of plasmid (final plasmid concentration >6 nM) into the thawed aliquot, avoiding pipetting as much as possible.
Transfer the mixture to an ice-chilled, 1 mm gap electroporation cuvette.
Electroporate at 1.25 kV, 400 Ω, and 25 μF.
Add 1 mL of room temperature MRS broth to the cuvette and mix by inverting once or twice.
Place the cuvettes into a static incubator at 37 °C for 2.5-3 hours to allow recovery.
Plate the entire amount onto multiple MRS agar plates with appropriate selection.
Add a small lit candle ("tealight") and an anaerobic atmosphere-generating sachet inside the container.
Grow the plates in a completely airtight container at 37 °C for 2-3 days or until visible colonies are present.
Pick any colonies required for measurement and inoculate into a 96-well storage microplate with 1.5 mL of filter sterilized MRS broth per well and an appropriate selection antibiotic.
Incubate the plate aerobically overnight at 37 °C without shaking.
Resuspend the overnight L. reuteri culture via pipetting.
Transfer 200 µL of resuspended culture into a flat, clear-bottom, 96-well plate.
Measure OD and fluorescence of mCherry2 (excitation: 589 nm; emission: 610 nm) in the plate reader.
Transfer 5 µL from the 96-well storage microplate to a PCR tube.
Spin down the sample until the pellet can be seen, discard the supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 20 μL of 20 mM NaOH.
Boil the sample at 95 °C for 5 min, vortex, and repeat boiling once more.
Chill the boiled samples on ice as much as possible to prevent template degradation and PCR inhibition.
Spin down the boiled samples to pellet cell debris.
Take 1 μL of supernatant and dilute into 99 µL of ice-cold DNase- and RNase-free ddH2O (100x dilution).
Use the 100x diluted sample as template DNA in a standard PCR reaction using plasmid-specific primers.
Include a positive control with a plasmid derived from E. coli mini-prep.
Return samples on ice after PCR and add an appropriate loading dye at 1x concentration.
Run a 1% agarose gel in TAE buffer at 110 V for 30 min.
Image the gel if necessary.
Inoculate L. reuteri into 10 mL of MRS broth containing an appropriate antibiotic.
Incubate overnight aerobically at 37 °C in a static incubator.
Centrifuge the culture at 5,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Wash the pellet with 2 mL of standard P1 buffer.
Discard the supernatant after centrifuging again at 5,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the pellet in 250 µL of modified P1 buffer containing 10 mg/mL lysozyme and 100 U/mL mutanolysin.
Incubate the suspension at 37 °C for 1-2 h.
Add 250 µL of buffer P2 to the lysed cells, mix by inverting four to six times, and incubate at room temperature for no longer than 5 min.
Add 350 µL of buffer N3 to the mixture, invert gently four to six times to mix.
Centrifuge at 10,000 x g for 10 min.
Transfer as much supernatant as possible to a spin column and centrifuge at 10,000 x g for 60 s.
Discard the flow through after spinning.
Wash the spin column with 500 µL of buffer PB.
Centrifuge again at 10,000 x g for 60 s.
Discard the flow through.
Wash the spin column with 750 µL of buffer PE.
Centrifuge at 10,000 x g for 60 s.
Discard the flow through and centrifuge again for 60 s to remove residual buffer.
Place the spin column in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Apply 20-30 µL of DNAse- and RNAse-free ddH2O to the filter of the spin column.
Leave for 1-2 min before centrifuging at 10,000 x g for 60 s.
Perform a standard PCR reaction using plasmid-specific primers.
Include a positive control with a plasmid derived from the E. coli mini-prep.
